controls_that_must_fail_the_hypothesis.rule90_is_blind_to_the_lag_set: D_n(h) = 1 at every one of these lags, so this control cannot detect a wrong lag set; only the Sturmian one can

sturmian_fibonacci.note: Aperiodic, uniquely ergodic, exact frequencies to infinity: the density of ones is 1/phi^2 = 0.381966 and D(1)/(N-1) = 2/phi^2 = 0.763932 exactly, since the word has no 11 factor. It is the only control here that is aperiodic while having uniform averages, which is the regime P2 occupies, and the only one whose answer moves with h.

registered_kill_is_uncalibrated.eligibility: the kill compares the two largest prefixes, so a lag needs h <= N/2 at two of them; lags above 2^21 are reported at N = 2^23 only and can never fire it
registered_kill_is_uncalibrated.note: The kill named no magnitude, so it fires on the sign of a mean-zero statistic. Every observed z is inside the range these null samples produce, and the below-half count is at chance. Recorded as a design error in the registration, not rescoped after the fact.

registered_control_deviation.note: The h=12 half is not reproduced and the difference is a statistic mismatch, not a disagreement: the prior audit records C-densities and this script reports D-ratios, linked by C = (n-h) - 2D. At h=6 the two agree only because 1/3 is the fixed point of x -> 1 - 2x, so that agreement was a coincidence and not the cross-check the registration intended. Disclosed here; the registration is left as written.

aggregate_alternative_3.statement: limsup_N (1/N) sum_(0<=i<j<m) C_N(2^j-2^i) <= 0 for an unbounded set of m

power_against_common_mode_bias.model: D_N(h)/(N-h) = 1/2 - eps at EVERY lag of the pair set simultaneously
power_against_common_mode_bias.gain_is_lag_dependent: sqrt(sum_pairs (N-h) / (N-h0)) varies with the reference lag h0; see the per-m gain range, and note it is NOT sqrt(k), which would need every N-h equal

aggregate_alternative_3.note: Two directions, and they are opposite. Against a COMMON-MODE bias present at every lag, the aggregate pools the signals linearly while the null sd grows only in quadrature, so it is more sensitive than any single lag by sqrt(sum_pairs (N-h)/(N-h0)), a factor that depends on the reference lag. Against a bias localized to ONE lag it is LESS sensitive by exactly the same factor, that lag's signal being pooled with the others' noise. Hypothesis (2) fails if a single h fails, so the per-lag test is the correct instrument for (2) and this aggregate for (3); a single lag failing does NOT refute (3), since other lags may cancel it. A clean aggregate therefore does not certify (2) UNIFORMLY over alternatives, though against the common-mode class specifically it is the sharper of the two tests. Neither constrains a limsup at any finite N. A sign-agnostic triangle bound k max|C_N|/N is available but is the wrong tool, (3) being one-sided: it discards the signs the statement is about. At fixed m that bound tends to 0 anyway, k being constant in N.

scope: One trace, one statistic, four prefixes. Can only kill; ratios at or above 1/2 confirm nothing, since no finite N establishes a liminf. The per-lag resolution floor is 1/(2 sqrt(N-h)), so a liminf below 1/2 by less than that is invisible here and this run does not distinguish the hypothesis from its negation.
